# TinyStories260K UART hardware acceptance client

This module implements the host-side deployment and acceptance protocol for the independent HX1P35A user SPI NOR and UART. It first validates the project's simulation and full TD implementation evidence, requires a passing programming report with bitstream hashes exactly matching the TD report, and verifies both pinned model assets plus the firmware CRC contract before opening a serial port.

The client speaks 115200 baud, 8-N-1. It checks the user Flash JEDEC ID, optionally uploads the 1,056,540-byte checkpoint using the monitor's W frame and stop-and-wait 256-byte page acknowledgements, then issues V and requires the complete image CRC to match. It sends the fixed T diagnostic request and independently compares all 1536 FP32 logits within absolute tolerance 0.002 and checks each argmax and emitted TOKEN line. It tokenizes a story prompt using tok512.bin BPE with BOS and a dummy leading space, sends G plus token IDs, then independently verifies every emitted token against tinyllm.Reference. The board performs every inference step; the host only handles tokenization/decoding and runs the independent verifier.

UART interactions are deadline-bounded: 240 seconds per line, 30 seconds per flash page acknowledgement, and 30 minutes total for diagnostic and generation inference. The transcript and a fail-status hardware report are persisted for failures; hardware status becomes pass only after JEDEC, CRC, diagnostic logits/argmax, and story-token checks all pass. The module supports pyserial COM/tty ports and the provided FTDI D2XX URI transport. It does not invoke a downloader/programmer, manipulate FPGA configuration Flash, or modify drivers.

Local validation parsed the Python source, loaded the pinned tokenizer, checked UTF-8 fallback tokenization, confirmed the prompt token sequence, exercised the T and G response parsers against independent Reference-generated frames, and verified diagnostic predictions for prompt IDs [1, 382]. No serial device was opened in this implementation turn; physical acceptance requires valid programming evidence and an operator-provided port.
checks: Preflight uses simulation_valid and implementation_valid, then requires programming status pass and exact bitstream_hashes equality with the TD report.
Validates pinned stories260K.bin and tok512.bin SHA-256, 1,056,540-byte image size, and firmware MODEL_CRC32 before serial open.
Implements 115200 8-N-1 UART via pyserial or FTDI D2XX, JEDEC check, optional stop-and-wait W upload with per-page plus acknowledgement, and full-image V CRC validation.
T diagnostic checks three positions and all 1536 FP32 logits against independent NumPy Reference at absolute tolerance 0.002, including argmax/TOKEN results.
G generation uses tok512.bin BPE with BOS/dummyspace/UTF-8 byte fallback, enforces ctx64 bounds before serial open, and compares emitted token sequence against independent Reference.
Provides per-line, page-ack, and total inference deadlines; saves UART transcript and hardware.json failure record on runtime exceptions.
Local AST, tokenizer, UTF-8 fallback, checkpoint-size, T/G fake UART parser, and Reference diagnostic checks passed; no serial device or physical hardware was accessed.
